result.title: CogniLife: Continuous Cognitive Distillation for Deployed Multi-Expert Agent Marketplaces
result.summary: Multi-expert agent marketplaces -- where creators publish domain-specific AI experts for end users to consult -- are an emerging deployment pattern for language technology. A published expert can receive many requests yet little evidence about its creator, who remains active elsewhere: the cold-expert problem. We frame continuous cognitive distillation as converting attributed creator observations into revisable decision rules, communication patterns, and domain procedures. CogniLife proposes a cross-expert attribution design for this problem, with Creator Profiles for transferable creator patterns and Expert Journals for listing-specific knowledge; this design is not yet implemented or evaluated. A deployed platform partially realizes the surrounding lifecycle through creator-authorized authoring, capability-owned proposal filtering, and reversible consolidation of eligible owner-scoped memory. On ProfyBench-v1, an 85-task offline benchmark built from replay seeds and controlled internal tests, the Profy Full configuration as a whole achieves a mean overall score of 4.65/5 from the primary LLM judge, compared with 4.01 for Raw LLM and 4.28 for Expert Prompt, with the largest gains in completeness, specificity, and missing-information tasks. These configuration-level scores do not test cold-expert mitigation, cross-expert transfer, or longitudinal distillation.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文面向多专家 agent 市场中的「冷专家」问题，提出将创作者观察转化为可修正的决策规则、沟通模式与领域流程的持续认知蒸馏框架，并以 Creator Profiles 和 Expert Journals 为设计；其中跨专家归因设计尚未实现或评估，仅平台生命周期部分落地，另用 85 题离线基准给出配置级评分。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「将观察序列蒸馏为可修正规则」及能力归属过滤、可撤销记忆合并的机制，可能为 LVR 中轨迹训练、贡献分配与状态更新提供概念参照，但论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理，需较多核查。
